I think it's very very strange. I haven't kept up with it but the cover-up and censorship army seems awfully organized and expansive, it seems off.

My (wild, baseless) conspiracy theory is that the last year showed us widespread testing of new internet censorship and control systems..

The JTRIG slides showed a sophisticated understanding of social networks and how they can be used to turn crowds of people to a goal, mentioning strategies such as creating fake accounts to act as victims to give credence to some story or another.. That's part of the GamerGate angle, then there's the censorship.

We also had the release of all those celebrity nudes. I'm not saying this is what happened, but if you had an internet censorship system set up and you wanted to test its effectiveness against an "information bomb," a piece of information so virulant that it would be guaranteed to spread like wildfire.. You couldn't have picked a better package. And we know who has the easiest access to these celebrities' photos. Maybe it was a hacker, a hacker that worked for the NSA.

It's going nicely. About as well as I had hoped for. I did a lot at the start of it. To explain people what needed to be done and what should be avoided. It's showing people how deep corruption is rooted and how many people are jerking each other off. It's useful.

its the poultice the gaming industry has needed for years

So Unity 5 just came out last week. Have any of you guys given it a try yet? How different is it from Unity 4.6? Is it worth it to upgrade? Is it harder to use than 4.6?

Been using it for a week.

Not harder, but they have moved some things around so there are some growing pains.

It does seem more resource heavy. I've heard people's projects requiring as much as 30% more juice after porting to 5. Most of that seems to come from the new shader and lighting system.

I've run into a few very annoying bugs but I'm not sure they are U5 specific. For about 4 days my raycasts weren't detecting Mesh or Box colliders, but would see Sphere or Capsule, then it randomly fixed itself. Also for some reason Freeze Rotation doesn't want to lock down rotation after two colliders collide, again it could just be me. (I eventually just wrote my own constraint script)

But all that said, it looks gorgeous. The new shader system is awesome. You can import Blender files directly now (my older version did not, not sure if that is new to U5 or something I missed by not updating) so that's great.

All in all I love it, but it does seem to be more resource heavy.

Hmm, I think I'll stick with 4.6 for a while until the bugs are dealt with in that case. I do look forward to the new lighting and shaders however. I hear you can have stuff with reflections now, is that true? Is the basic water any better?

I haven't played with water, but the new metallic physics based shader is amazing.

The you put a reflection node on it and BAM fully mirrored reflections from within the scene. (again, resource heavy)

This gets into it pretty well. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eGu9_8HS2uI
Does all of that come with the free version or Unity 5 Pro? Oh man, I want to try it so bad now.

YES! The engine is 100% complete in the Free version!

I know I've been DYING for post processing, then they give me THIS!

I've been using the Blender's Cycles Render with Nodes, which now imports a hell of a lot better with the new Shader system.
Damn. Now I'm even more tempted to migrate. I'll see how well they manage to patch up those bugs in the next couple of weeks.

I know the raycast issue is pre-5, as most all of the help threads I saw about it were older than 5.

The constraint issue might be new, but a script works better (lets you add min and max and recover over time).
